title: Introduce Residency Quarantine Gatekeeper and Delegation Telemetry for RBACv2
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers operating across multiple jurisdictions occasionally surface ambiguous region claims from upstream services (missing/contradictory region headers or stale residency assertions). These cases increase compliance risk and complicate KMS routing and audit retention. This PR introduces a lightweight control plane component (Residency Quarantine Gatekeeper) plus RBACv2 delegation telemetry hooks that together: 1) automatically quarantine requests with conflicting or absent residency assertions, 2) emit high-fidelity delegation telemetry to help SRE/security triage suspicious operator flows, and 3) annotate KMS proxy calls with immutable locality context to improve auditability without changing key material.

Summary of changes: Adds gatekeeper and feature-flagged rollout path, RBACv2 instrumentation (delegation telemetry), and audit-sampling profiles that increase retention for quarantined flows. Also includes a small operator-honeypot detector used only for telemetry and alerting (no automated revocations). All behavior is behind the new feature flag security.residency_quarantine.

Design notes: The gatekeeper runs as a policy middleware in the API ingress path. It evaluates (in order) explicit region claims, tenant pinned-region metadata, and operator-delegation traces. If evaluation yields ambiguity or contradictions, the gatekeeper either: (a) mark request as QUARANTINED and forward to normal processing while tagging audit metadata and increasing sample rate, or (b) short-circuit and return 409 with an explanatory header when the tenant policy requires strict enforcement. The KMS proxy accepts an additional signed-locality header (populated by gatekeeper) for richer provenance but does not change key selection logic. Delegation telemetry emits a compact tuple (operator_id, delegate_chain_hash, policy_path, decision_timestamp) to the secured telemetry stream for SRE review.

Small snippet (policy evaluation logic, illustrative):
if regionHeader == "" && tenantPinned == "" {
  // Ambiguous — mark for quarantine and increase audit sample
  ctx.Metadata.Put("residency.status", "QUARANTINED")
  audit.SampleRate.Bump(ctx.RequestID, 100)
}

Rollout plan: feature flag default=off. Staged rollout to: dev -> staging (10%) -> prod (shadow mode) -> prod (enforce 1%) -> prod (enforce broader) per playbook in docs/compliance/residency_quarantine.md. If any false positive spike in errors >3% QoS, rollback to shadow mode and revert sampling change only.

Testing: Added unit tests covering 8 evaluation permutations, e2e tests simulating tenant pinned-region mismatch, and a small load harness that validated additional middleware adds <0.8ms median and <2% p99 tail at 500 RPS.

Security and compliance considerations: The gatekeeper adds no new key material and does not persist sensitive payloads. Delegation telemetry is PII-minimized (operator_id is hashed at source, full operator lookup only available to authorized analysts). KMS locality header is signed with service signing keys and validated by the proxy; signature proof is included in audit logs. Threat model reviewed by security (SEC-710) and notes attached in Linear.

Backwards compatibility: No customer-visible API changes except optional 409 responses for tenants that opt into strict quarantine in their policy. All other behavior is additive and behind a flag.

Related work: Complements ENG-2145 (operator delegation audit) and SUP-4321 (support ticket: ambiguous region claims causing KMS misrouting).
